Subject: MAP: security acceptance appendix & retention commitments

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I pulled together a short security appendix we propose to attach to the mutual action plan so Pangea has a clear acceptance runway tied to SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ responses, and DPA redlines. Key points below and attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (control coverage snapshot), sig-caiaq-export.xlsx (completed questionnaire), and an annotated DPA draft (dpa-redlines-v3.docx).

High level proposed acceptance gates (suggested dates in parentheses):
- Evidence intake & review (Week 1–2): we provision targeted SOC 2 artifacts and CAIQ items; Pangea security reviews.
- Staging evaluation (Week 3): sandbox integration with synthetic data; acceptance criteria: request/response latency, key rotation test, and audit log visibility.
- Legal/Contract sign (Week 4): finalize DPA redlines and sign.
- Production go/no-go (Week 5): successful staging sign-off + contract signature.

Data retention specifics you asked about: Redwood hosts customer data in hosted (multi-tenant) or dedicated pools. For the MAP we propose retention tiers: 30 days (request logs and temporary KV cache), 90 days (access logs), and 7 years (contractual audit logs, with escrow option). We can surface per-route retention controls and a separate annex for EU residency if needed.

Next steps I propose:
1) Pangea security confirms which SOC 2 artifacts are required for initial review (e.g., SOC 2 type II full report or snapshot + complementary evidence).
2) Pangea legal provides a single prioritized DPA redline doc; we’ll respond inline.
3) Schedule a 45-min staging checklist review on Wed/Thu (propose Wed 10/11 morning PT).

Looping Ben (account lead) and Laura (legal) for visibility and so we can turn around DPA redlines quickly.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Karthik Iy er

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick follow. This looks promising and aligns with where our security team wants to land. A few clarifying items from our side before the staging call: 

1) For SOC 2, we need either the full Type II report (preferred) or a Type II + evidence bundle covering user access controls and logging. If you can provide a signed report, that speeds legal review.

2) Retention: we expect a default maximum retention of 90 days for request/response payloads in hosted deployments unless there is a specific business need and a DPA annex. Are you able to commit to a 90-day default for hosted? If not, we will push for it in the DPA. 

3) Data residency: any production traffic for EU customers must remain in EU regions. For our initial POC most traffic will be US. If Redwood offers dedicated pools scoped to a VPC, please confirm sequencing for those options in the MAP.

Attached is a Pangea redlines file (will share via procurement separately).

Wed 10/11 10:00am PT works for our security + infra folks. Please send calendar invite.

Best,

Alice / Team —

Appreciate the clarity. A few concrete answers from our side to feed into the MAP and the staging checklist: 

- SOC 2: Redwood can provide the signed SOC 2 Type II report for our hosted offering and a controls evidence bundle (user access, change control, backup procedures). I’ll attach the SOC 2 summary in the invite; full report will be shared under NDA if required.

- Retention: We can commit to a 90-day default for request/response payloads in hosted by default. For customers requiring shorter windows we expose per-route TTL controls. For audit logs and billing records we retain 7 years unless explicitly agreed otherwise. We’ll add a retention annex to the DPA specifying per-class defaults and escalation for exceptions.

- Data residency / Dedicated: Dedicated pools (VPC) are available; sequencing in the MAP: initial hosted POC (Week 1–4) -> Dedicated pool onboarding (parallel legal/infra work, target Week 4–7) -> production cutover. Dedicated onboarding typically requires a short connectivity window and a single maintenance cutover.

Our proposed acceptance criteria for staging:
1) Evidence bundle delivered and acknowledged by Pangea security.
2) Sandbox integration: API key rotation, request/response traceability, and audit log retention verified.
3) Latency & throughput: meet agreed SLOs for 95th percentile latency for MAP test suite.

Laura — can your team review the attached DPA redlines (dpa-redlines-v3.docx) quickly and flag any must-haves so we can get to procurement sign-off?

I’ll send the invite for Wed 10/11 10:00am PT and include a short agenda.

Thanks,

Alice / Ben / Karthik —

Thanks — quick confirmation from legal: we’ve reviewed Pangea’s initial procurement redlines (received via procurement) and provided in-line replies in dpa-redlines-v3.docx. High level: 

- Retention: Redwood accepts the 90-day default for request/response payloads in hosted and will include a retention annex for route-level overrides.
- Data residency: we acknowledge EU residency requirement; for customers requiring EU-only hosting we’ll scope a dedicated pool or EU-operated hosted region and include residency language in an annex.
- Audit & evidence access: Redwood will provide granular audit logs on a rolling 90-day basis in the console, with an export capability for longer-term retention on request. For contractual audit events we will provide a secured export (encrypted) within the agreed SLAs.

We’ve added two small legal asks to the DPA: 
1) Mutual indemnities: narrow to proven breaches resulting from Redwood platform failures (proposed language in doc).
2) Subprocessor list & notification timing: we propose a 30-day prior notification window for additions.

If these look acceptable we can get procurement to prepare a signature-ready DPA and aim for Week 4 sign-off in the MAP.

Laura Bennett
